items.title: Clyde Kerr Jr. interviewed by Monk Rowe, Rome, New York, August 22, 2006
items.q: I remember like one of the last funerals I attended was a great friend of mine, an old guy by the name of Waldron “Frog” Joseph

ctx.x: So that’s what you’re hoping comes back.

Yeah, yeah. From all walks of life you know. If you’ve ever been to New Orleans and attended a jazz funeral in New Orleans, you know like some of the old time jazz musicians, when they pass, it’s always at that time when I attend one of those and I listen to the music, I listen to the musicians come together to play and the singers coming together to sing, and watch the people coming in from all types of walks of life. It’s then that I realize why I stayed in New Orleans all my life. That particular thing. It’s…
Yeah. There’s nothing like it anywhere else I bet.
